format.description: High spelling error rate (>3%) is a strong indicator of poor quality or AI-generated text. Such errors can severely undermine credibility and indicate lack of human oversight.
Frequent double spacing (>4 occurrences) typically reflects minor formatting sloppiness. It has minimal direct impact on authenticity but suggests careless editing.
Irregular fonts indicate potential copy-paste or tampering across multiple sources. This poses a moderate-to-high credibility risk and may signal inconsistent or manipulated document origins.
Having more than three font sizes suggests inconsistent structure or merging of multiple documents. This contributes to perceived document unreliability and reduces readability.
Inconsistent indentation often results from poor editing or manual tampering. While it affects readability, it also hints at possible document manipulation.

When both high spelling errors and inconsistent formatting occur, the document shows signs of careless or automated generation. These combined issues compound credibility concerns and raise suspicion of low-quality or synthetic authorship.

The simultaneous presence of irregular fonts, multiple font sizes, and inconsistent indentation suggests significant visual and structural instability. Such inconsistency implies possible content merging or tampering.

When multiple minor hygiene issues appear together — spelling errors, spacing irregularities, and inconsistent sizing — they collectively indicate a systemic lack of attention to detail and poor document hygiene.
